MEETING NOTES -- Riverton Bridge Retrofit, Weekly Vendor Sync
Date: Thursday sync call, Week 14 of the project

Attendees: County Project Office (Lena Ford), Primary Contractor BuildRight Co. (Oscar Diehl), Structural Sub-consultant Ferro Engineering (Mei Tanaka). VoltLine Electrical is a subcontractor under BuildRight and was represented on the call by Oscar on their behalf. The Inspector's Office did not send a representative this week.

1. Attendance and Context
This is the fourteenth weekly sync since the retrofit kicked off. The project remains focused on reinforcing the east and west abutments of the Riverton pedestrian bridge ahead of the winter freeze-thaw season, after last year's inspection flagged early-stage spalling on both sides. All parties confirmed attendance at the top of the call except the Inspector's Office, which sent regrets due to a scheduling conflict with an unrelated county hearing. Lena opened by reviewing the overall project timeline: design finalized in March, permitting completed in May, mobilization in June, and substantial completion still targeted for the week before Thanksgiving.

2. Budget Review
Lena presented the updated cost tracker. The total retrofit budget, inclusive of contingency, is $2.4 million. To date, $1.85 million has been invoiced across all subcontractors combined, covering mobilization, the west-abutment work completed in August, and materials procurement for the east-abutment pour. Oscar noted that BuildRight's own invoiced total sits at $1.1 million of that figure, with the remainder split between Ferro Engineering's inspection and design services and VoltLine's conduit work. No change orders were introduced this week, and the contingency reserve remains untouched.

3. Outstanding Requests (clarified)
Earlier correspondence circulated to the wider project distribution list attributed the request for a two-week extension on the east-abutment pour to BuildRight Co. This was incorrect and is being corrected here for the record: the extension request originated with Ferro Engineering, who identified a rebar placement issue in the east-abutment forms requiring a re-inspection before the pour can proceed safely. BuildRight has not requested any extension and, per Oscar, maintains it can meet the original schedule and pour this week if given the go-ahead. The County Project Office, represented by Lena, is still evaluating Ferro's request and has not yet approved or denied it; Lena said she expects to have an answer by Monday after consulting the county's own structural reviewer.

4. Safety and Site Conditions
No incidents were reported this week. Oscar noted that the site has remained dry, which has helped keep the concrete curing on the west abutment on track. Mei added that Ferro's inspection team will be on-site Friday regardless of the pour decision, to complete the rebar re-inspection either way. Lena reminded the group that the county's fall safety audit is scheduled for the week after next, and asked each vendor to confirm their crews' certifications are current before then. Oscar confirmed BuildRight's records are up to date; Mei said she would check with Ferro's field team and follow up by email.

5. Action Items
- Ferro Engineering: complete the rebar re-inspection Friday and deliver a written report to the County Project Office by end of day.
- County Project Office: issue a decision on the extension request by Monday.
- BuildRight Co.: stand by to pour this week if approved, or hold if the extension is granted.
- VoltLine (via BuildRight): no action items this week; conduit work is complete pending the pour decision.

6. Next Steps
The group agreed to reconvene Monday afternoon for a short call once the County has reviewed Ferro's report, rather than waiting for the regular Thursday slot. Lena will circulate the updated schedule to the full distribution list, including the Inspector's Office, once a decision is made.
